source.title: Towards Interpretable Protein Structure Prediction with Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Nithin Parsan; David Yang; John J. Yang

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Conceptually tests whether removing the SAE reconstruction residual loses downstream model behavior by evaluating ESMFold with SAE-reconstructed representations. It does not measure the error geometry or scaling described in the original claim.
record.gate_note: The CASP14 reconstruction results bear on V5: the study replaces the layer-36 representation with its SAE reconstruction and reports structure-prediction outcomes. It does not test linear predictability, tokenwise error scaling or overlap across SAE sizes, matched-size random errors, the two proposed error components, or whether SAE training artifacts explain the error. Feature-steering results do not compare behavior with and without the error term and are not rows for these versions.
record.test_reason: The study is weak evidence and is not about dark matter as such. In a new setting (ESM2-3B into ESMFold), it splices the layer-36 SAE reconstruction in place of the activation and reports structure-prediction accuracy, which bears on whether discarding the SAE error loses model behaviour (V5). It does not measure error linearity, error scaling, matched random errors, error components or training-artifact causes.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that SAE reconstructions of ESM2-3B preserve ESMFold structure-prediction accuracy and language-modeling performance at moderate-to-high L0, while full embedding ablation degrades structure prediction. They also report that Matryoshka SAEs match or beat TopK and L1. They do not frame any of this in terms of SAE error or dark matter.
record.recipe_differences: Evaluates downstream structure prediction after SAE reconstruction rather than measuring error-vector linearity, token-level error scaling, context overlap across SAE sizes, or matched-size random errors.
record.method_sensitivity: Representation condition changes the result: layer-36-only and SAE-reconstructed layer 36 maintain performance, while full embedding ablation degrades it.
record.code_released: The paper says code, dataset, pretrained models, and a visualizer will be released upon publication; URL not stated.
record.problems: The structure evaluation uses 17 of 34 CASP14 targets after filtering by sequence length and baseline ESMFold prediction quality. It does not compare SAE reconstruction errors with random errors of matched size or directly test any proposed dark-matter structure.
record.rows_left_out: No other reported results directly test the claim versions. Feature-steering SASA and GRAVY outcomes do not measure whether the SAE error term matters.

untested.parts: Linear predictability of the SAE error from the input activation.
Per-token error-norm prediction across SAE sizes, shared failing contexts, and persistence of error with scale.
There is no comparison of reconstruction-induced loss against random errors of the same norm.
There is no split of the error into linear and nonlinear parts and no test of their learnability.
No circuit or steering analysis is run with and without the error term. The steering case study never adds the error back.
There is no test of whether error stems from training choices or shrinks with end-to-end training. The TopK/Matryoshka/L1 ΔCE comparison is not framed around dark matter.

missing.what: ΔCE between original and SAE-reconstructed ESM2-3B at layer 18 across sparsity for TopK, Matryoshka and L1: about 2.5–3.0 at L0<10, near 0 above L0 100, and L1 worse at higher L0.
missing.versions: V5 (and loosely V6 for the architecture comparison)

missing.what: CASP14 ΔRMSD between ESMFold and SAE reconstruction across sparsity K; structure is reasonably recovered with about 8–32 active latents.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is about building SAEs for protein models, and its fidelity evaluations only incidentally bear on V5. Three things weaken the structure result: CASP14 was filtered to 17 of 34 targets, dropping those where ESMFold RMSD exceeded 10 Å; the spreads are large; and there are no significance tests. The proper comparator for the SAE condition is layer-36-only, not unablated ESMFold. The architecture ΔCE comparison (L1 vs TopK/Matryoshka) is the study's own method compared with others, so it is not counted as a V6 test.

versions.untested_parts: Whether a large share of the SAE error vector is a linear function of the input activation.
Per-token error-norm predictability across SAE sizes, same-context failures across sizes, and whether error persists with scale.
No comparison of model loss after SAE reconstruction against random errors of the same size.
No separation of linear and nonlinear error components or tests of their feature content and learnability.
Tests structure-prediction behavior using SAE reconstruction, but not circuit analyses, steering behavior with and without the error term, or explicit error-term inclusion.
No test of whether error is caused by SAE training choices or shrinks with improved architectures or end-to-end training.

rows.subject: ESMFold
rows.operation_detail: Used the layer-36 SAE reconstruction as the representation supplied to ESMFold and ablated other ESM2 layers.

conditions.value: layer 36 SAE reconstruction; other ESM2 layers ablated

rows.measure: Backbone RMSD between experimental structures and predictions
rows.note: The authors describe the SAE reconstruction as maintaining comparable structure-prediction performance. The aggregate is over 17 CASP14 targets.
rows.check: The right baseline is the layer-36-only ablation (r2, 2.9 ± 2.1 Å), not unablated ESMFold. Against it, SAE reconstruction gives 3.2 ± 2.6 Å, a 0.3 Å rise well inside the spread over 17 targets. The targets were pre-filtered to drop those where ESMFold RMSD exceeded 10 Å.

source_check.correct: SAE reconstruction: 3.2 ± 2.6 Å. Matched layer-36-only ESMFold control: 2.9 ± 2.1 Å. Unablated ESMFold: 3.1 ± 2.5 Å.
source_check.problem: The supplied baseline is accurately transcribed but changes the layer-ablation condition; the matched control for the reconstruction intervention is layer-36-only ESMFold.

rows.subject: ESMFold
rows.operation_detail: Kept only the layer-36 representation and ablated other ESM2 layers, without SAE reconstruction.

conditions.value: layer 36 only; other ESM2 layers ablated

rows.measure: Backbone RMSD between experimental structures and predictions
rows.note: The authors describe this condition as maintaining comparable performance. Aggregate over 17 CASP14 targets.
rows.check: This is the layer-ablation control with no SAE involved. It sets the baseline for r1 and does not measure the SAE error's effect.

rows.subject: ESMFold
rows.measure: Backbone RMSD between experimental structures and predictions
rows.note: The authors state that full ablation significantly degrades performance. Aggregate over 17 CASP14 targets.
rows.check: Full ESM2 embedding ablation is a capability control unrelated to the SAE error term. It should not be linked to V5.

rows.subject: ESMFold
rows.operation_detail: Compared predictions using SAE reconstruction with ESMFold predictions, with layer 36 used in both.

conditions.value: SAE reconstruction and ESMFold, both using layer 36

rows.measure: Backbone RMSD between ESMFold and SAE predictions
rows.note: The authors say this similarity confirms preservation of structural information. Aggregate over 17 CASP14 targets.
rows.check: No baseline is given. A mean 3.1 Å (SD 4.4) divergence between layer-36-only and SAE predictions is comparable to the error against experiment. This suggests some targets change substantially, so it cannot be read as 'no effect'.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.2 and Figure 2b, ESMFold versus SAE with both using layer 36

relationships.condition: ESMFold structure prediction on 17 filtered CASP14 targets, Matryoshka SAE on ESM2-3B layer 36, compared with layer-36-only ablation
relationships.reason: Replacing layer 36 with its SAE reconstruction raises RMSD only from 2.9 to 3.2 Å (r1 vs r2). Little structure-prediction accuracy is lost without the error term. This is weak evidence: targets were filtered, r4 shows nontrivial divergence between predictions, and the label rests on r1 alone.
relationships.display_finding: Reconstruction increased RMSD from 2.9 to 3.2 Å on 17 filtered targets, although comparisons between predictions showed nontrivial divergence.
